sentences.text: Neptunidraco was an extinct carnivorous marine crocodilian that lived during the Middle Jurassic.
The type specimen, which serves as the basis for the species, consists of a partial skeleton with an incomplete skull and lower jaw preserved in nodular limestone.
This fossil represents the most complete metriorhynchid known from Italy.
The remains were recovered in the 1950s near Portomaggiore, Italy.
Italian paleontologists Andrea Cau and Federico Fanti formally named the genus Neptunidraco in 2011.
Before this formal description, the specimen was referred to as an unnamed species of the genera Metriorhynchus or Geosaurus.
Neptunidraco is the oldest known member of the metriorhynchid family of fully marine reptiles.
It belongs to the subfamily Geosaurinae, which consists of large marine predators adapted to open-ocean life.
The animal lived in what is now northeastern Italy.
The time range for Neptunidraco is estimated from 170.9 to 143.1 million years ago.
